newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: Bullion price woes dominated South African shares on Monday as the sliding price of the yellow metal gave local gold stocks a hammer blow that reverberated into the wider market, dealers said.
The latest collapse of bullion, sparked by news that Australia has sold gold reserves, saw the price dip to fresh twelve year lows below $318 an ounce.
Many analysts are predicting bullion will break through support at $310 and even launch an assault on $300. The gloomy predictions saw blood spilled across the local gold index.
The index dropped 48.2 points, or 5.06 percent, to 903.9 as dealers realised the price fall was threatening the country's industry. The index is at its lowest since February, 1993.

"They (the traders) are calling it down to below $300 and if it does go to that there will be only three, four or maybe five mines in South Africa (who can produce profitably)," said Leon Esterhuizen, gold analyst at Societe Generale Frankel Pollak.

Sentiment took a further knock as Randgold said its East Rand Proprietary Mines Ltd (ERPM) unit was going to close it Benoni Gold Mining Co Ltd due to the price fall. Randgold ended down 305 cents to 16.90 rand as ERPM lost 15 cents to 112 cents.

Randgold also said due to "current market conditions" it was reviewing the ratios of the proposed merger between its Durban Roodepoort Ltd, Blyvooruitzicht Gold Mining Co Ltd and Buffelsfontein Gold Mines Ltd.
Durban lost 150 cents to 14.00 rand, Blyvooruitzicht shed 10 cents to 230 cents and Buffelsfontein dropped 67 cents to 938 cents.
Dealers said the gold index was likely to go down further. "The gold index has just bombed out and it isn't over yet," one dealer said.
The gold market's woes flowed out into the wider market and dented sentiment in the industrials index. Industrials ended off 58.9 points to 8,743.0 as the all-share slid 74.8 points to 7,293.2.

Dealers added that the market was also being hit by a much-needed correction after recent strong gains and a period of window-dressing prompted by the unit trust quarter end and the futures close-out.
They predicted the market would now seek to consolidate around these levels. "The market will probably try and hold itself around here," one dealer said.
Overall, 138 shares ended up against 223 which fell. Volumes were quiet with just 570 million rands worth of shares changing hands.

Amongst individual counters to catch the market's interest was Baobab which gained 600 cents to 62.00 rand on news it had upped its stake in specialist financial services firm Theta Securities (Pty) Ltd and would move to the banking sector on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE).

New-listing Prospur Packaging PURJ.J failed to draw a single trade after its unbundling from Harwill Investments Ltd. Dealers said that the lack of interest stemmed from Harwill's general inactivity and confusion following the complex transactions accompanying the float.

Asean Investment Corp Ltd dipped sharply on worries over the firm's annual financial statements after the JSE said its listing was under threat of suspension and possible termination because it had failed to submit its annual financial statements on time. Asean lost 11 cents, or 35.48 percent, to 20 cents.
Futures dealers, having supported the market with healthy spot buying in recent weeks, were conspicuous only by their absence on Monday and contracts trailed equity downwards.
The gold September contract was last at 628/35 from 668 as the industrials was at 8,504/15 from 8,630. The all-share contract was 6,672/87 from 6,766.
